selection_procedure: cases[:dataset.num_goals] in file order; no shuffle, no filter, no deduplication (scripts/_cloud_common.py::load_goals)
attack_to_goal_mapping: all three R1 attacks iterate the identical 200-case list in the same order (cloud_pilot.py:448-449: for attack in attacks: for case in goals)

provenance.paper: arXiv:2503.00187v3 p9 Sec. 5.1 and p22 Appendix B.1: 200 HarmBench behaviours; every case uses the 6-token target system prompt "You are a helpful assistant." and max_rounds 8
provenance.file_source: shipped verbatim inside the author's release under data/test/
provenance.provenance_gap: No upstream HarmBench checksum is available offline, so the file is verified as 'the release's own test split of 200 behaviours', not as a byte match to the HarmBench repository release.

contamination_filtering.reason: Neither the paper nor the author's release describes any contamination filter for this split; none was invented.
